claim: This test is a test used in diagnosing the disease "Clostridium difficile colitis".
context: diagnosis: Stool testing algorithm (GDH screening, toxin EIA, NAAT) — CDI is confirmed with a multi-step stool testing algorithm: a sensitive glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH) or nucleic-acid amplification test (NAAT) screen, combined with a toxin A/B enzyme immunoassay (EIA) to distinguish active toxin-mediated infection from asymptomatic carriage of toxigenic strains. Only unformed (diarrheal) stool should be tested. A GDH-positive, toxin-negative result can be arbitrated by NAAT for the toxin genes. The IDSA/SHEA approach is the same, except that NAAT alone can be considered diagnostic when stool samples are appropriately selected.

loinc_label: Heparin Ab [Presence] in Platelet poor plasma by Platelet aggregation
claim: This test is a test used in diagnosing the disease "heparin-induced thrombocytopenia".
context: diagnosis: Functional platelet activation assay — A functional test - serotonin release assay or heparin-induced platelet activation test - that measures whether the patient's serum actually activates platelets, and does so in the heparin-dependent pattern. It is the reference standard precisely because it interrogates the pathogenic property rather than mere binding, and it is what distinguishes autoimmune HIT, where activation persists without heparin but is still inhibited at high heparin concentrations.

loinc_label: Borrelia miyamotoi DNA [Presence] in Blood by NAA with probe detection
claim: This test is a test used in diagnosing the disease "Borrelia miyamotoi disease".
context: diagnosis: PCR with GlpQ serologic support — Acute infection is confirmed by PCR detection of B. miyamotoi DNA in blood or CSF. Serologic testing against GlpQ can support relapsing-fever Borrelia exposure, but GlpQ assays do not distinguish hard-tick B. miyamotoi disease from soft-tick relapsing fever. Antibody to recombinant GlpQ is usually absent at presentation and present in convalescent sera, so PCR on blood is the acute test and serology confirms on later or paired samples. Standard two-tier B. burgdorferi (Lyme disease) serology met seropositivity criteria in only 10% of infected patients in the series a review summarizes, while GlpQ antibody separates relapsing-fever infection from Lyme disease.

context: diagnosis: Confirm HIV Infection and Differentiate HIV-1 from HIV-2 — AIDS classification first requires established HIV infection. Contemporary multitest algorithms include differentiation of HIV-1 and HIV-2. In the U.S. laboratory testing algorithm, specimens are screened with an HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody (fourth-generation) immunoassay; a reactive screen reflexes to an HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation immunoassay, and a negative or indeterminate differentiation result is resolved with an HIV-1 nucleic acid amplification test, the step that identifies acute HIV-1 infection.
